questions.question_text:
For a fleet of machines, the correlation coefficient between hours of maintenance per month and the number of faults recorded is $r = -0.93$.
How is this association best described?

options.text: Strong negative
Strong positive
options.why: Reads the size $0.93$ correctly as strong but drops the minus sign, so the direction is reversed.

options.text: Moderate negative
options.why: Keeps the negative direction but places $0.93$ in the moderate band; a size above $0.75$ is strong.

options.text: Moderate positive
options.why: Drops the minus sign and also places $0.93$ in the moderate band, so both the direction and the strength are wrong.

questions.solution_text:
$r = -0.93$ is negative, so faults tend to fall as maintenance hours rise.
$0.93$ lies between $0.75$ and $1$, so the association is strong.
The association is strong negative.

questions.question_text:
In a survey of cafes, the correlation coefficient between the number of seats and the average wait time is $r = 0.42$.
How is this association best described?

options.text: Weak positive
Moderate positive
options.why: Keeps the positive direction but places $0.42$ in the moderate band; a size below $0.5$ is weak.

options.text: Weak negative
options.why: Reads the size $0.42$ correctly as weak but reverses the direction of a positive $r$.

options.text: Moderate negative
options.why: Places $0.42$ in the moderate band and also reverses the direction, so both the strength and the direction are wrong.

questions.solution_text:
$r = 0.42$ is positive, so wait time tends to rise as the number of seats rises.
$0.42$ is below $0.5$, so the association is weak.
The association is weak positive.

options.why: Reads the strength from the spread correctly but reverses the direction of a rising trend.
Treats any visible scatter as meaning almost no association.
Ignores how far the points sit from a straight line and assumes an almost perfect fit.

questions.solution_text:
The points rise from left to right, so $r$ is positive.
They are spread around the trend rather than lying close to a line, so the association is moderate rather than strong.
Of the values offered, $0.65$ is the best approximation.

questions.question_text:
Across $25$ countries, chocolate eaten per person and the number of Nobel prizes per million people have $r = 0.79$.
Which conclusion is valid?

options.text: There is a strong positive linear association, but the data cannot show that eating chocolate causes Nobel prizes.
Eating more chocolate causes a country to win more Nobel prizes.
options.why: Treats a correlation coefficient as proof of cause and effect.

options.text: There is no association, because chocolate cannot possibly affect research output.
options.why: Denies a genuine statistical association because the causal story sounds implausible.

options.text: Because $r$ is positive, no confounding variable such as national wealth can be involved.
options.why: The sign of $r$ says nothing about whether a third variable explains both.

questions.solution_text:
$r = 0.79$ is positive and above $0.75$, so the association is strong and positive.
A correlation coefficient measures association only, so no causal claim follows; a confounding variable such as national wealth could raise both figures.

questions.question_text:
For $18$ regions, the correlation coefficient between spending on public transport and the percentage of commuters driving to work is $r = -0.84$.
What does this indicate about the relationship?

options.text: There is a strong negative linear association: regions with higher public transport spending tend to have a lower percentage of commuters driving to work.
There is a strong positive linear association: regions with higher public transport spending tend to have a higher percentage of commuters driving to work.
options.why: Uses the magnitude $0.84$ correctly but ignores the negative sign and reverses the direction.

options.text: There is a weak negative linear association: regions with higher public transport spending tend to have a lower percentage of commuters driving to work.
options.why: Keeps the negative direction but treats a magnitude close to $1$ as weak.

options.text: Increasing public transport spending will definitely cause the percentage of commuters driving to work to fall.
options.why: Treats the negative correlation as proof of a causal effect.

questions.solution_text:
$r = -0.84$ is negative, so the percentage of commuters driving to work tends to fall as public transport spending rises.
$|r| = 0.84$ lies between $0.75$ and $1$, so the association is strong.
This indicates a strong negative linear association, without establishing cause and effect.

questions.question_text:
A dataset comparing daily exercise time and resting pulse rate has $r = -0.87$.
Which statement correctly describes the association?

options.text: Strong negative: resting pulse rate tends to fall as daily exercise time rises.
Weak negative: resting pulse rate tends to fall as daily exercise time rises.
options.why: Treats a negative coefficient as weak instead of using its magnitude $0.87$.

options.text: Strong positive: resting pulse rate tends to rise as daily exercise time rises.
options.why: Uses the magnitude correctly but drops the minus sign and reverses the direction.

options.text: Moderate negative: resting pulse rate tends to fall as daily exercise time rises.
options.why: Places $|r| = 0.87$ in the moderate band even though it is above $0.75$.

questions.solution_text:
$r = -0.87$ is negative and $|r| = 0.87$ is above $0.75$.
There is a strong negative linear association: resting pulse rate tends to fall as daily exercise time rises.
